nodes.name: FORCE platform
nodes.description: Dyne's proprietary platform for developing therapeutics that address the root cause of disease. The platform consists of an antigen-binding fragment (Fab), a linker and a payload rationally designed to target the genetic basis of the disease being treated. The Fab binds transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) to enable delivery to muscle and the central nervous system. Dyne states that a Fab offers advantages over a full antibody, including enhanced tissue penetration, increased tolerability and reduced risk of immune system activation. The linker is chosen based on payload chemistry, and payloads include antisense oligonucleotides, phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers, small interfering RNA and biologics. Stated potential advantages include delivery to muscle and CNS, extended time between doses and the ability to re-dose.

nodes.name: Zeleciment rostudirsen
nodes.description: An investigational therapeutic for individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy who have mutations in the DMD gene amenable to exon 51 skipping. It is not approved for commercial use in any jurisdiction. It consists of a phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer conjugated to an antigen-binding fragment that binds transferrin receptor 1, designed to enable production of near-full-length dystrophin in muscle and the central nervous system, and is administered intravenously every four weeks as proposed in the submitted Biologics License Application. A Biologics License Application for potential U.S. Accelerated Approval has been accepted by the FDA and granted Priority Review.

nodes.name: Zeleciment basivarsen
nodes.description: An investigational therapeutic for people living with myotonic dystrophy type 1. It is not approved for commercial use in any jurisdiction. It consists of an antisense oligonucleotide conjugated to an antigen-binding fragment that binds transferrin receptor 1, designed to reduce toxic nuclear DMPK RNA, release splicing proteins and allow normal mRNA processing.

additionalProperty.name: Development stage
additionalProperty.value: Investigational; evaluated in the Phase 1/2 ACHIEVE and Phase 3 HARMONIA clinical trials

additionalProperty.name: Approval status

additionalProperty.name: Mechanism of action
additionalProperty.value: Reduction of toxic nuclear DMPK RNA. An antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) payload is delivered to muscle and the central nervous system via an antigen-binding fragment (Fab) that binds transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1), releasing sequestered splicing proteins and allowing normal mRNA processing.

additionalProperty.name: Regulatory designations

nodes.name: DYNE-302
nodes.description: An investigational therapeutic in clinical development for people living with facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy. It is not approved for commercial use in any jurisdiction. It consists of an antigen-binding fragment that binds transferrin receptor 1 conjugated to an siRNA designed to reduce DUX4 expression. The FDA cleared the Investigational New Drug application on July 28, 2026, allowing a Phase 1 trial to begin; DYNE-302 is Dyne's third program to enter clinical development.

nodes.name: Duchenne muscular dystrophy
nodes.description: A rare, X-linked and progressive neuromuscular disorder and the most common childhood-onset form of muscular dystrophy. Loss of strength and function typically first appears between 3 and 5 years of age.
nodes.epidemiology: Affects approximately 12,000 people in the United States and approximately 16,000 people in the European Union.

cause.name: Mutations in the DMD gene
cause.description: Mutations in the DMD gene lead to total absence or nearly undetectable levels of dystrophin protein, which is essential for muscle structure, function and preservation.

signOrSymptom.name: Progressive muscle weakness, typically beginning in the hips, pelvis and upper legs before progressing to the shoulders, arms, trunk, neck and other muscle groups
Cognitive function impairment and neuropsychiatric disorders, including intellectual disability, learning disability and behavioral difficulties
Delays in developing motor skills such as sitting, standing or walking

nodes.name: Myotonic dystrophy type 1
nodes.description: A rare, progressive, genetic neuromuscular disease with high morbidity and early mortality. Symptoms can begin at any point in life depending on subtype; adult-onset symptoms typically appear between 20 and 40 years of age. Severity and rate of progression vary.
nodes.epidemiology: Affects approximately 40,000 people in the United States and approximately 55,000 people in the European Union.

cause.name: Mutations in the DMPK gene
cause.description: Mutations in the DMPK gene lead to widespread disruption of RNA splicing, known as spliceopathy, which drives the multi-system manifestations of the disease.

signOrSymptom.name: Cognitive impairments, excessive daytime sleepiness, fatigue and dysregulated sleep

nodes.name: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy
nodes.description: A rare, progressive, genetic disease caused by aberrant DUX4 expression in muscle, with consequent damage and loss of function. Age of onset varies widely; symptoms typically begin to appear in the teen years or early adulthood.
nodes.epidemiology: Affects approximately 15,000 to 40,000 people in the United States and approximately 20,000 to 50,000 people in the European Union.

cause.name: Aberrant DUX4 expression
cause.description: Individuals with FSHD carry a genetic mutation that allows the DUX4 gene to be sporadically activated in muscle cells, causing their gradual destruction throughout the body.

signOrSymptom.name: Loss of facial muscle strength, making it difficult to smile or use a straw
Progressive weakness in the arms, torso, legs and abdomen

nodes.name: Pompe disease
nodes.description: A rare metabolic muscle disease associated with the GAA gene.
nodes.epidemiology: Affects approximately 4,500 people in the United States and approximately 5,500 people in the European Union.

page.description: Active Dyne Therapeutics clinical trials in Duchenne muscular dystrophy and myotonic dystrophy type 1, with trial designs, endpoints and Dyne's patient access policy.

nodes.name: HARMONIA
nodes.description: A global, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, confirmatory Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the efficacy, safety and tolerability of zeleciment basivarsen in people living with myotonic dystrophy type 1. The trial will enroll approximately 150 participants age 16 and older, randomized 1:1, who will receive 6.8 mg/kg of z-basivarsen or placebo once every eight weeks for 48 weeks. Participants who complete the placebo-controlled period may enter a long-term extension and receive 6.8 mg/kg every eight weeks for up to 24 additional weeks. The primary endpoint is change from baseline in the five times sit to stand (5xSTS) test at week 49. Secondary endpoints include video hand opening time, quantitative muscle testing, the 10-meter walk/run test, the Myotonic Dystrophy Health Index, and additional patient- and clinician-reported outcomes.

nodes.name: ACHIEVE
nodes.description: A global, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind Phase 1/2 clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of zeleciment basivarsen in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1. The multiple ascending dose portion resulted in selection of a registrational dose and regimen of 6.8 mg/kg administered every eight weeks. A registrational expansion cohort to support potential regulatory submissions, including Accelerated Approval in the U.S., is fully enrolled. The primary endpoint for that cohort is change from baseline in middle finger myotonia as measured by video hand opening time (vHOT) at 6 months, compared to placebo.

nodes.name: FORZETTO
nodes.description: A global, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, confirmatory Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the efficacy, safety and tolerability of zeleciment rostudirsen in ambulatory male participants with Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping. The trial will enroll approximately 90 participants 4 to 18 years of age, randomized 1:1, who will receive 20 mg/kg of z-rostudirsen or placebo once every four weeks for 72 weeks. Participants who complete the placebo-controlled period may enter a long-term extension and receive 20 mg/kg once every four weeks for up to an additional 96 weeks. The primary endpoint is change from baseline in rise from floor (RFF) velocity at week 73. Secondary endpoints include stride velocity 95th centile, North Star Ambulatory Assessment total score, 10-meter walk/run velocity, four-stair climb velocity and forced vital capacity percent predicted, as well as additional functional and patient-reported outcome measures.

nodes.name: DELIVER
nodes.description: A global, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind Phase 1/2 clinical trial that evaluated the safety, tolerability and efficacy of zeleciment rostudirsen in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy who have mutations in the DMD gene amenable to exon 51 skipping. The multiple ascending dose portion resulted in selection of a registrational dose and regimen of 20 mg/kg administered every four weeks. The placebo-controlled portion of the registrational expansion cohort has been completed; its primary endpoint was change from baseline in dystrophin protein levels as measured by Western blot at 6 months. Participants from the multiple ascending dose and registrational expansion cohort portions had the option to enroll in the open-label extension and long-term extension portions of the study.

nodes.name: DYNE-302 Phase 1 trial in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy
nodes.description: A randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multiple ascending dose Phase 1 clinical trial of DYNE-302 in ambulatory adults ages 18 to 65 living with facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy. The FDA cleared the Investigational New Drug application on July 28, 2026. The first group will enroll 9 participants who will receive three intravenous doses administered every four weeks, randomized 2:1 to DYNE-302 1.5 mg/kg or placebo; higher doses and less frequent administration are to be evaluated afterwards. Participants who complete the placebo-controlled period may enter an open-label long-term extension in which all participants receive DYNE-302 for up to an additional 96 weeks. The primary objective is safety and tolerability; additional objectives cover pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and DUX4-related biomarkers in muscle and blood, including muscle DUX4 transcriptome changes and plasma levels of the protein KHDC1L.
